places.name: Khô Mộc Tự
places.size: A small ruined temple of a fallen sect: about 25 broken halls and cells in a compound about 150 m across around a huge withered tree; a few dozen monks at its height; empty since 641.
places.where: Region 1/2, temperate forest at about 150 m, in a deep unbroken conifer forest (on the map an unmarked carpet of dark pines with a pale grassy patch at the left). Former sect, small, fallen; held by Lãng Đạo Môn's river country. Nearest: Thủ Mộ Thôn 103 km, Tịch Tĩnh Lâm 160 km. The abbot, who had played the zither in the pines, withered with his tree in 641; something there is still playing.
places.imagined: A grey still dawn. The roofs of the little temple have sunk, a vast bare trunk with grey branches stands in the middle of the court, and a thin sound of a zither seems to come from the ruin.
places.subject: The place: Khô Mộc Tự, the Withered Tree Temple, a ruined small temple in a deep forest. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; an unbroken carpet of dark pines fills the frame with a few pale grassy pockets, a faint overgrown path running in from the lower left. The ruin: in a small clearing about one hundred and fifty metres across stand about twenty-five broken halls and monks' cells of grey stone and timber, their grey tile roofs half collapsed, walls green with moss, a gate hall fallen across the path, small courtyards grown thick with bracken and birch saplings, and a low surrounding wall in gaps. Signature element: in the centre of the court stands one huge withered tree, grey and bare, thirty metres tall with a trunk so wide that twenty people could not ring it, its branches spread like a skeleton hand over the roofs, with a pale ring of bare ground around its base where nothing grows; at its foot a flat stone with a small broken zither-shaped hollow, and a few tiny grey-green wildflowers. The pines around the clearing lean slightly away from it. Fallen roof tiles lie in drifts along the old walls, and a few bare ribs of roof timber show through the gaps. Life at scale: none; one tiny figure standing alone at the stone, and a mist rising from the roofs. Light and season: cold grey dawn in late autumn, thin golden light from the upper left on the bare tree, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Cầm Tượng Trấn
places.size: A ruined zither-makers' town of about 300 houses once, now half buried under a ravine wall in a footprint of about 600 m by 250 m; buried in 1012 and left, the makers moved to an academy's rim.
places.where: Region 1, pine sea highlands at about 470 m, temperate forest; on the map rocky crags and tors rising through a forest of pines and green glades. Former town held by Vạn Hác Viện, Wood 33 %, Metal 26 %. Nearest: Thải Sâm Trấn 103 km, Tiều Phu Thôn 112 km, Vạn Hác Viện 125 km. The makers' unfinished zithers are down there under the fall, and their dead.
places.imagined: A quiet noon light. A great grey wall of fallen rock has slid across half the town, roofs sticking out of it, and in the open half the workshops stand with their doors ajar and racks of zither blanks.
places.subject: The place: Cầm Tượng Trấn, the Zither-Makers' Town, a mountain town half buried by a ravine wall. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a country of pale rocky crags and tors rises through a forest of pines and green glades, a deep ravine running across the middle of the frame, its far wall raw and pale. The ruin: about three hundred workshops and houses of timber and stone with grey tile roofs along a long street on the ravine's near side; the upper half of the town is buried under a great tongue of broken grey rock and splintered trees that fell from the ravine wall in 1012, roofs sticking out of it at all angles, a pagoda leaning in the rock; the lower half stands, doors ajar and roofs half collapsed, tall lofts with racks of long seasoned wood still visible in the open sheds, a long drying yard with weathered frames, a stone bridge over the ravine's stream broken. Signature element: on the open side, long rows of drying racks hold hundreds of unfinished zither blanks, pale slabs of wood in regular ranks, weathered grey; and on the rock fall itself a single cairn with a tiny string of silk strung between two posts that glints. Life at scale: nobody lives here; one tiny searcher with a lantern at a gap in the rock, a mule. Light and season: quiet late-morning light in autumn, warm golden from the upper left on the pale rock, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Thải Chi Cốc
places.size: A minor sect of herb growers and alchemists, about 120 people (most of them children), founded 480: a valley of about 800 m by 300 m with some 50 buildings (drying sheds, dormitories, a lingzhi hall), striped herb beds and a slim three-roofed pagoda; small, busy and green.
places.where: Region 1, a shallow forest valley of the Nine-Bend River (Cửu Khúc Xuyên), temperate forest at about 20 m; on the map a wide bay of blue water at the upper edge, a grassy ridge with brown rocky slopes, a river winding down to the lower right. Vassal of Tùng Đào Cung, righteous, Water 40 %, Wood 29 %. Nearest: Độc Điệt Trạch beast lair 79 km. Founded by lingzhi pickers who had left the world.
places.imagined: Morning planting. The valley floor is striped with herb beds in green, ochre and dusky purple stepping down to the river, and at the valley mouth four moss-grey stone hermits sit in a row, each holding a lingzhi, judging who may enter.
places.subject: The place: Thải Chi Cốc, the Lingzhi-Picking Valley, a herb-growing sect in a shallow forest valley. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a shallow forested valley opens at the left of frame onto a river that bends along the lower edge, a wide blue bay at the top, brown rocky slopes and a grassy ridge around, and dense forest at both sides. The valley: its floor is striped with herb beds in bands of green, ochre and dusky purple, stepping down toward the river, hundreds of strips, edged with narrow paths and irrigation channels; among the beds stand about fifty buildings, low grey-tile drying sheds with open sides hung with bunches of herbs, dormitories, a long lingzhi hall, a grinding house, a children's school yard with small figures, and a gate hall at the valley mouth; at the valley head terraces climb to a slim three-roofed pagoda, the tallest outline. Signature element: at the valley mouth, four moss-grey stone hermits sit in a row beside the road, each cradling a lingzhi in its lap, facing the road, each three metres high, with moss on their shoulders. Life at scale: dozens of tiny children in grey working in the beds with baskets, a line walking down the paths to the river, women at the drying racks, smoke from a boiling shed. Light and season: bright early summer morning, golden light from the upper left on the herb stripes and the stone hermits, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Lãng Đào Môn
places.size: A ferrymen's sect of about 150 boat people, mostly mortal crew, founded 790: a compound of about 45 tarred timber buildings on a gentle rise about 400 m across, with rope sheds, a landing and a gate made of two boat hulls about 18 m tall; small but loud with river trade.
places.where: Region 1, low wooded ground near the Nine-Bend River, temperate forest at about 10 m; on the map a blue bay at the upper right, a rocky hill peninsula, a river winding at the left and lower right. Vassal of Tùng Đào Cung, Water 30 %, Wood 41 %. Nearest: Phá Chu Trấn ruin 103 km, Tẩy Sa Tuyền 103 km. It carries most of the river trade.
places.imagined: Late afternoon. A gate of two great upturned boat hulls stands on end, keels meeting overhead, dark with tar; behind it timber halls and rope sheds climb a rise, and a path of crushed shell runs to the landing where barges lie.
places.subject: The place: Lãng Đào Môn, the Wave-Rider Gate, a ferrymen's sect on low ground near a river. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; low wooded ground fills the frame, a river bending in blue loops at the left and lower right, a blue bay at the upper right with a rocky grass-brown hill in front of it. The compound: about forty-five buildings of dark tarred timber with grey tile roofs climbing a gentle rise, a training yard with a full-size boat deck laid on the ground for lessons in water arts, rope sheds with coils like giant bobbins, oar racks, a long dormitory, a mess hall and a three-roofed hall on the top of the rise; stacks of oars and coiled rope in the yards. Signature element: the sect gate at the front of the compound is formed by two great river-boat hulls, dark-tarred, each about eighteen metres long, stood on end on stone footings with their keels meeting overhead in a pointed arch; a path of crushed white shell runs from the arch down to the landing. Along the landing lie a dozen big river barges and ferries with long sweeps, one in a slip being tarred. Life at scale: tiny crew carrying rope and oars, a line of loaded carts at the landing, children practising rowing on the deck, smoke from the tar kettles. Light and season: late afternoon in summer, golden light from the upper left on the white shell path and the tarred hulls, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Đào Thanh Thành
places.size: A walled river city of about 18,000 roofs and perhaps 90,000 people, walls about 2.6 km by 2 km, quays set high up the bank on tall stone steps; a timber and resin trade city under pine forest.
places.where: Region 1, northern river bank under endless pine, temperate forest at about 80 m; on the map a river running diagonally from the upper right through dark forest to the lower left, rocky hills with pale ridges on both sides. Tùng Đào Cung city founded 300. Nearest: Đào Âm Mạch spirit vein 75 km, Thạch Lâu Thôn 177 km. A flood in 700 drowned three quays.
places.imagined: A windy evening. The townsfolk climb the walls to hear the pine waves roar over the city, while at low water a row of old drowned quay pillars stands in the current like a broken fence.
places.subject: The place: Đào Thanh Thành, the Pine Wave city, a walled river city under endless pine. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a broad river runs diagonally across the frame from the upper right to the lower left, dark pine forest rising at both banks to the edges and rocky pale ridges at the left and lower right. The city: a rectangular wall of grey stone about two and a half kilometres long on the left bank with a three-storey gate tower the tallest outline, enclosing some eighteen thousand grey-tile roofs in tight rows, a city hall with green-glazed eaves at the centre, timber yards and resin warehouses along the wall, long stacks of squared pine logs, resin boiling yards with smoke, markets, courtyard houses of the families of outer disciples, and a broad avenue running up toward the pine ridge. Along the river edge tall stone stair-quays climb the bank in a long row with stacked barrels; just off the quays a line of broken old quay pillars stands in the shallow current like a broken fence, the old river line from before the flood, with a few swimmers' marks. Dozens of timber barges and rafts moored. Signature element: the pillars in the water and the pine forest crowns above the wall bending visibly in waves of wind. Life at scale: porters on the quays, ox teams with logs, townsfolk on the walls facing the wind, a raft being poled. Light and season: windy evening in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the wall and the pine crowns, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Đào Sa Thị
places.size: A sprawling stilt market of about 800 low houses and stalls with no wall, perhaps 4,000 people, across tidal sand flats about 1.5 km long, with about 300 gold-washing cradles in the shallows; one signal mast about 35 m tall.
places.where: Region 1, river mouth sand flats on the coast at sea level, temperate forest; on the map a wide bay of blue water at the upper edge, grassy brown rocky hills, the river winding at the lower right and left. Tùng Đào Cung market, Water, Wood. Nearest: Bạch Dương Lâm 127 km, Phá Chu Trấn 150 km, Lãng Đào Môn 160 km. Founded around 800 by gold-washers; the Ferry War burned the landing in 1173.
places.imagined: Low tide at midday. The whole flat glitters with fine gold, washers in wide straw hats rock their cradles in rows in the shallows, and the charred ribs of burned ferries lie along the landing.
places.subject: The place: Đào Sa Thị, the Gold-Washing Sand market, a stilt market on golden sand flats at a river mouth. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a broad river mouth spreads into golden sand flats and shallows at the centre of the frame, a wide blue bay at the top, brown and grassy hills behind, the river winding down at the lower right and left. The market: no wall; about eight hundred low houses and stalls of grey tile and thatch on posts, in loose clusters linked by plank walkways, across the flats; a central open market of scales, sieves and awnings, a customs hall, lodging houses, a gold assayers' row with small stone strongrooms, and boat landings; one tall tarred signal mast about thirty-five metres high on a pier is the tallest outline. Signature element: across the shallows, in rows by the hundred, small wooden washing cradles on stilts, each rocked by a tiny washer in a wide straw hat, and wherever the water has drained the sand glitters with fine gold; along the landing lie the charred black ribs of burned ferries, left as a memorial, with scorched posts. The shallows are a patchwork of brown water and bright sand, and the plank walkways cast dark straight shadows over it. Life at scale: hundreds of tiny washers, brokers weighing gold on tiny scales, boats of ore sand, children carrying buckets. Light and season: midday at low tide in early autumn, bright golden light from the upper left making the sand flats glitter, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hà Bạn Trấn
places.size: A low riverside town of about 1,100 roofs inside a modest rectangular wall about 450 m by 300 m, roughly 5,000 people, open to the river, with a great waterwheel about 12 m across; a herb-mill and shipping town of the valley.
places.where: Region 1, bank of the Nine-Bend River at about 20 m, temperate forest; on the map a river bending in sharp zigzag across a forest of dark green and olive, a small pale ground marking the town on its left bank. Held by Thải Chi Cốc. Nearest: Cự Miết Chử beast lair 75 km, Cựu Hà Trấn ruin 127 km. A hamlet until 290 when the river's new course ran past its door.
places.imagined: A busy morning of loading. The waterwheel turns and creaks at the upstream corner, grinding roots into powder, and herb sacks stand stacked on the short jetties waiting for boats.
places.subject: The place: Hà Bạn Trấn, the Riverside town, a herb-mill town on the Nine-Bend River. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a dense forest of dark green and olive fills the frame, a river bending in sharp angles from the upper middle to the lower left, a faint pale road leading to the town on the river's left bank. The town: a low grey-tile town of about eleven hundred roofs inside a modest rectangular wall about four hundred and fifty metres long, open on the river side where about a dozen short jetties reach into the water; fishing lanes all end at the river; rows of low houses, a central square with a granary, herb warehouses with open doors, a grinding yard with sacks. Signature element: at the upstream corner stands a great dark timber waterwheel about twelve metres across beside a long mill house, turning in a diverted stream with white water, the tallest outline; stacks of herb sacks sit on the jetties, and three flat boats are moored. Small boats and fish traps along the shore. The river is dark green and slow above the wheel, and white and fast below it. Life at scale: porters carrying sacks, a line of carts on the road from the valley, women sorting roots on mats, children fishing off a jetty. Light and season: bright morning in early autumn, golden light from the upper left on the wheel and the water, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Lâm Hạ Trấn
places.size: A small walled town of about 1,000 roofs inside a wall about 400 m by 300 m, roughly 4,500 people, so deep under old beeches that the roofs are green with moss; with about 40 round granaries on mushroom-shaped stone staddles.
places.where: Region 1, northern forest by a river, temperate forest at about 60 m; on the map a deep forest of beech green and a river curving down the middle, rocky pockets at the lower left. Tùng Đào Cung granary town, Wood, Water. Nearest: Thử Vương Cương beast lair 79 km, Hạc Quy Thôn 150 km. Tùng Đào set its northern granaries here in 600.
places.imagined: Noon in cool green shade. The roofs are moss-green under the beech crowns, round granaries with conical roofs stand on mushroom stones so no rat can climb them, and the lanes smell of grain dust.
places.subject: The place: Lâm Hạ Trấn, the Beneath-the-Woods town, a granary town hidden under old beeches. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep forest of old beeches fills the frame to every edge in rounded green crowns, a river curving down the middle as a bright ribbon, pale rocky pockets at the lower left. The town: a low cluster of moss-green grey-tile roofs inside a small rectangular wall about four hundred metres long, almost hidden under the broad crowns of the beeches, so that the roofs show only in gaps; narrow lanes, a central square with a well and a granary master's hall, coopers' yards, and gates on the river and forest sides. Signature element: among the houses stand about forty round timber granaries with conical roofs, each raised on squat stone staddles shaped like mushrooms about a metre high, in rows along the lanes and in two big yards, so no rat can climb them; their pale conical roofs stand out as little tents among the green. Life at scale: a few tiny granary-keepers on ladders, a cart of sacks at the gate, cats on the staddles, coopers rolling barrels. Light and season: noon in late summer, warm golden light from the upper left breaking through the beech crowns in pockets, dappled shadows, long soft shadows toward the lower right. At the town's centre a small square holds a well-house, a bell post and a long open hall where the grain is weighed, and the lanes between the granaries are lined with barrels, coopers' stacks of staves and woven rat-traps hung on poles. The river passes beside the wall with a plank landing where grain barges tie up, and a thin road runs out through the beeches, so deep in shade that a cart on it shows only as a pale gleam in the gaps.

places.name: Tuyết Ốc Thôn
places.size: A village of about 20 half-sunk turf-roofed houses with a tall red door-pole before each, perhaps 100 people, in about 200 m.
places.where: Region 1, upper river valley, temperate forest at about 30 m; on the map a river valley between dark forest slopes with pale rocky pockets at the lower left and right. Tùng Đào village. Nearest: Thâm Tuyết Lâm forest 90 km, Sài Môn Thôn 127 km. Deep winters; houses half under the snow since 340.
places.imagined: Deep winter. The village almost vanishes: grassy mounds under snow, chimneys smoking through the drifts, a forest of tall thin red door-poles the only colour.
places.subject: The place: Tuyết Ốc Thôn, the Snow-House village, a village half buried by winter snow. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a snowy upper river valley between dark pine slopes, the river a narrow dark thread with ice at its edges winding to the right edge, pale rocky pockets at the lower left and right. The village: about twenty low half-sunk houses with turf and grass roofs under snow drifts, clustered tightly beside the river, each with a short tunnel entrance, smoke rising from short chimneys through the drifts, narrow trenches cut through the snow between doors, a snow-covered woodstack and small fenced pens. Signature element: over each house rises a tall thin red-painted door-pole, three metres high, a little forest of red vertical lines taller than the roofs, the only strong colour in the white landscape; some poles have fresh red paint, one newly painted bright. Life at scale: a few tiny villagers digging a trench, children sliding on a bank, a woman painting a pole, a dog in a trench. Light and season: deep winter late afternoon, golden light from the upper left on the snow and the red poles, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right. The upper river beside the village is a narrow dark channel running between wide white snow banks, with a plank bridge buried to its rails. A few sleds stand upturned in the drifts, a stack of winter firewood forms a long white-capped wall behind the houses, and the dark spruce at the valley's edge carries heavy loads of snow on every branch. The red poles are slightly different heights, so that they trace the slope of the ground like a scatter of red hairs.

places.name: Hàn Mai Thôn
places.size: A snowy village of about 12 grey-roofed houses round a small square with one winter plum, perhaps 60 people, in about 150 m.
places.where: Region 1, riverbank, temperate forest at about 20 m; on the map a river winding through a deep forest, a pale small clearing at the upper left. Tùng Đào village. Nearest: Dã Mai Lâm 75 km, Ngạo Tuyết Phái minor seat 202 km. In 420 a winter plum bloomed through the snow above a buried child.
places.imagined: A snowy dusk. One gnarled winter plum blooms red inside a low bamboo fence in the square, the only colour for days of travel, and villagers bow to it on the way to the river.
places.subject: The place: Hàn Mai Thôn, the Cold Plum village, a snowy village with a single blooming plum. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a snow-covered riverbank among dark forest, a river winding along the edge with shore ice, a pale small clearing at the upper left. The village: about twelve low grey-tile houses with thick snow on their roofs around a small snowy square, each with a small yard and woodpile, thin smoke rising, a narrow trampled path down to the river and a plank landing. Signature element: in the middle of the square grows one gnarled dark winter plum, its crown spreading about ten metres across and thick with bright red blossoms, inside a low bamboo fence, its fallen petals making a red ring on the snow; every path in the village leads to it. Life at scale: a mother carrying a newborn to the tree, three villagers bowing at the fence, a child with a sled, smoke. The plum's red is the only strong colour in the whole white and grey scene, and its petals lie in a thin scatter beyond the fence. Light and season: winter dusk, golden light from the upper left lighting the red blossoms, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right. A second smaller ring of footprints circles the fence, worn by bowing villagers. Short paths lead from every door to the plum like spokes. Beyond the river the dark forest stands still, with a pale low sun between its trunks.

places.name: Bạch Lang Thôn
places.size: A ring village of about 18 houses around a hollow, perhaps 90 people, in about 200 m; the hollow ringed with about 25 chalk-white boulders.
places.where: Region 1, river bend, temperate forest at about 40 m; on the map a river winding in sharp angles through dark forest. Tùng Đào village. Nearest: Lang Hồi Cương beast lair 75 km, Lâm Hạ Trấn 158 km. Built in 456 on the old den of the white wolf king slain by Thôi Khinh Hồng.
places.imagined: Spring liming day. The village circles a grassy hollow whose rim of boulders has just been limed white again, children run with wolf-tooth charms, and women beat laundry on flat stones at the river.
places.subject: The place: Bạch Lang Thôn, the White Wolf village, built around the den of a slain wolf king. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a forest of dark pines fills the frame, a river winding in sharp angles along the lower edge and right, a forest edge to one side. The village: a ring of about eighteen low houses of grey tile and thatch around a central grassy hollow about sixty metres across, each house with a small yard and wolf-pelt drying frames, a footpath from the hollow leading down to the river where flat washing stones lie in a row. Signature element: the hollow is rimmed by a circle of about twenty-five chalk-white boulders, freshly limed so they glow almost blue-white against the green grass, the stones as tall as a person; the hollow floor is bare earth and moss with a dark gap at one side, the old den mouth, now fenced with a low rail. Life at scale: three women beating laundry at the river, children running between houses, two men re-liming boulders with buckets, smoke from chimneys. Light and season: bright spring morning, golden light from the upper left on the white boulders, long soft shadows toward the lower right. The houses are low and thick-walled with turf-capped thatch, built shoulder to shoulder around the hollow so that their backs form a continuous curved wall, with only two narrow gaps for the paths. In the hollow's grass a few children's wooden toy swords lie scattered, and a stone cairn stands before the old den mouth hung with a long chain of wolf-tooth charms that glint in the light. The river beyond is a bright strip of cold water, and the washing stones are dark and wet.

places.name: Đông Lưu Thành
places.size: A mortal river city abandoned in 281 after the river left: about 3,000 roofs once, now stubs of walls over about 1.2 km by 0.8 km, with a quay wall about 600 m long; empty meadow and sand.
places.where: Region 1, great bend of the northern river, temperate forest at about sea level; on the map a lighter yellow-green meadow with faint old field lines at the left, a river winding in sharp angles through forest to the lower right. Former city held by Tùng Đào Cung. Nearest: Tân Lưu Trấn 79 km, Hà Đê Thôn 112 km. Built 90 by mortal boatmen; they fed the river spirit a pig every spring until it stopped answering, and ten years later the river left.
places.imagined: A golden dry afternoon. A long stone quay wall runs through an empty meadow with rusted iron rings hanging over grass, a fresh scar of sand where a spring flood opened an old paved street, and the living river far off.
places.subject: The place: Đông Lưu Thành, the City that the River Left, a mortal river city abandoned beside a dry river bed. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; an open meadow of pale yellow-green grass with faint ghost lines of old streets and fields fills the left of the frame, a wide dry river bed of sand, pebbles and tall grass running through the middle, and the living river visible at a distance at the right, a thin bright blue line winding in angles through dark forest. The ruin: the jagged roofless stubs of old warehouses and houses in rows over a wide area, about three thousand foundations visible as grey stone lines in the grass, long straight paved streets with grass in the joints, one city gate standing as two stumps; a short strip of uncovered paved street exposed by a spring flood as a pale scar of sand. Signature element: a long stone quay wall about six hundred metres long stands in the open meadow beside the dry bed, high as a house, hung with a row of rust-red iron mooring rings over the grass where boats once tied up, with a few tiny skeleton boat ribs in the dry bed. Life at scale: nobody lives here; three tiny old boatmen walking the quay wall, a heron in the dry bed. Light and season: late afternoon in autumn, warm golden light from the upper left on the quay wall and the meadow, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hổ Khiếu Cương
places.size: A long bare ridge about 20 km long with a crest banded like tiger stripes and a wind notch near the middle; no buildings, no path; one cave hollow among tumbled boulders.
places.where: Region 1/2, highland at about 980 m, between the bends of Cửu Khúc Xuyên; on the map a country of bare grey-ochre rock ridges and scree among green forest pockets. Beast lair, a great tiger (yêu cốt prize), belonging to no sect. Nearest: Thạch Khẩu Trấn 90 km, Cô Hạc Quán 90 km, Hổ Văn Khoáng 103 km.
places.imagined: Dusk. Wind funnels through a notch in the crest with a low growl, the crest is banded dark grey and pale ochre like a tiger's flank, and a real roar answers from the boulders below.
places.subject: The place: Hổ Khiếu Cương, the Tiger's Roar Ridge, a long bare highland ridge banded like a tiger. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a country of bare grey and ochre rock ridges and scree falls fills the frame with scattered dark scrub and small green forest pockets in the hollows, the long ridge running diagonally across the middle. Signature element: the crest of the ridge is banded in alternating dark grey and pale ochre rock in bold stripes across its width, like the stripes of a tiger's flank, each band tens of metres wide, repeating along kilometres of the ridge; near its middle a narrow notch cuts the crest, with wind-polished rock on its edges and a faint swirl of blown dust in it. Tumbled boulders and dark scrub on the flanks; among the boulders below, one shadowed cave hollow with a worn patch of bare ground at its mouth. No buildings, no paths; a faint grazing trail stops at the foot of the slope. A great tiger, a tiny tawny and black-striped speck, stands on a boulder above the cave hollow, its head raised mid-roar. Light and season: dusk in late autumn, low golden light from the upper left raking across the stripes, long soft shadows toward the lower right. Scree fans pour from the stripes in long pale and dark tongues, and the dark scrub clings in the hollows with a few lone stunted pines. The wind notch has a polished, scoured floor with a few small standing boulders in it, and from it a thin plume of blown dust trails downwind like a banner. Far below on the lowland edge a thin line of cattle and a rider's trail show how far the herders keep from the ridge.

places.name: Ngạo Tuyết Phái (the Plum Gate)
places.size: The old seat of a small sword sect of about 30 swordsmen and their families, founded 1105, now only the Plum Gate where every child's root is read in the first winter: a plum garden of about 200 trees, a gate and about 12 low buildings in about 250 m; a tiny gate and garden, not a hall.
places.where: Region 1, temperate forest at about 150 m; on the map a deep forest with a pale ridge at the lower left and a river winding in from the top, a pale grassy patch. Vassal of Tùng Đào Cung, Wood 52 %, Metal 9 %: a plum garden above Hàn Mai. The sect moved its sword hall to Thạch Khẩu Trấn in 1162. Nearest: Lâm Khẩu Thôn 112 km, Kiếm Xỉ Lĩnh 127 km.
places.imagined: A winter morning. In a garden of old plum trees in red flower, a plain grey gate stands; a row of children waits in the snow for their roots to be read, and a stern old swordsman turns one away himself.
places.subject: The place: Ngạo Tuyết Phái's Plum Gate, the first gate of a small sword sect in a plum garden. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep pine forest fills the frame, a river winding in from the top to the right edge, a pale rocky ridge at the lower left, snow lying in pockets. The garden: a clearing about two hundred and fifty metres across holds about two hundred old plum trees in uneven rows, in full red and pink flower, their blossoms bright against the snow; a plain grey plank gate under a small tiled roof stands at the garden's lower end on the road, its two posts marked only by wear, with a low fence of split bamboo, a small stone yard before it where children's roots are read, and about twelve low buildings of timber and grey tile, a gatekeeper's lodge, a tea hut, a small practice shed and a sword rack under a lean-to, set among the trees. Signature element: the plum garden in bloom and the plain gate with a line of about twenty tiny children and a few parents standing in the snow in single file before it, and one stern figure with a long sword at his back turning a child away at the gate. Life at scale: sword practice in the yard by four tiny figures, smoke thin from the tea hut, plum petals on the snow. Light and season: cold clear winter morning, golden light from the upper left on the blossoms, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Đoạn Vân Viện
places.size: A ruined cliff-hall academy of about 50 broken halls and galleries built on cliff ledges along about 700 m of mountainside, fallen in 1134; once a few hundred inhabitants, now rubble and silence.
places.where: Region 1/2, mountains at about 740 m, temperate forest; on the map a country of grey rock crags and ridges among pine forest with a river winding at the upper left. Former sect, held by Tùng Đào Cung, Wood, Earth. Nearest: Ưng Sào Nhai beast lair 79 km, Lăng Tiêu Các ruin 127 km. Its cliff halls fell in 1134; the survivors came to the pines; something under the fallen halls is alive, or pretending to be.
places.imagined: A grey spring afternoon. The cliff's upper ledges still hold half-halls hanging in air, the lower ones lie in a fan of rubble, and from the rubble a faint voice seems to answer every spring.
places.subject: The place: Đoạn Vân Viện, the Cloud-Cutting Academy, a cliff-hall ruin. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a mountainside of grey rock crags, bare ribs and scree rises among dark pine forest, a river winding at the upper left. The ruin: along a great pale cliff face about seven hundred metres long ran four tiers of ledges carrying about fifty halls, galleries and stairs of grey stone and timber with grey tile roofs, and in 1134 the middle of the cliff fell; now the upper two tiers survive only at the ends, halls hanging half over the drop with their floors broken off, covered galleries snapped, stairs ending in air; a great fan of rubble, broken roof tiles and beams spills from the gap to the valley floor, pale grey and brown, with a stone gate standing alone at its foot, one pillar fallen. Signature element: the fallen heap itself, a great scree fan strewn with pieces of carved cornice and roof ridge, and in its middle a dark hollow among slabs where something is alive; a thin path of cairns climbs from the lower right to the rubble's edge. The valley floor below the fan is green with spring grass, and thin streams of fine dust still slide from the rubble. Life at scale: none living; one tiny figure at the rubble's edge, a woman kneeling with a bunch of flowers, a few crows. Light and season: grey spring afternoon, thin golden light from the upper left on the pale cliff, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Thạch Khẩu Trấn (Ngạo Tuyết Phái's sword hall)
places.size: An empty ore town that a small sword sect (about 30 swordsmen and their families) has moved into since 1162: about 400 grey stone houses once, now about 120 repaired and the rest roofless, in a footprint of about 700 m by 400 m, with a sword hall and a forge; a small sect occupying a larger dead town.
places.where: Region 1/2, high mountain at about 850 m, temperate forest and bare grey rock ridges; on the map a jagged country of grey and white peaks among dark pine forest, a green meadow at the lower right. Held by Tùng Đào Cung, Wood 27 %, Metal 26 %, Earth 22 %. Nearest: Hổ Khiếu Cương 90 km, Thúy Trâm Phong 103 km, Hổ Văn Khoáng 112 km. The tiger-stripe ore ran thin and a spirit tiger took the last miners in 1161.
places.imagined: A cold clear morning in a grey mining town. A sword hall with a freshly tiled roof stands among roofless houses, a forge smokes, the sect's swordsmen practise on the old ore-yard, and spoil heaps striped like a tiger lie behind.
places.subject: The place: Thạch Khẩu Trấn, the Stone Mouth town, an empty grey ore town now the home of a small sword sect. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a jagged mountain country of grey and white peaks and ridges among dark pine fills the frame, a green meadow at the lower right, steep scree slopes between. The town: about four hundred grey stone houses of mining families in terraces up a steep valley, a long main street, an ore-sorting yard and a headframe over a shaft, with about one hundred and twenty of the houses repaired with fresh grey tile and the rest roofless and open to the sky, grass on their floors; a stone sword hall with a deep dark roof and a wide practice yard at the street's top, a forge with a thin smoke, a few vegetable plots in old yards, families' washing lines. Signature element: behind the town the spoil heaps of the old tiger-stripe ore, banded dark and pale in broad stripes, spill down the slope like a tiger's flank, and the sword hall's new roof stands out as the one dark clean line in the grey; a faint pale road winds in from the lower right. Life at scale: about eight tiny swordsmen practising in two rows in the yard, women at the washing lines, a child with a wooden sword, a smith at the forge. Light and season: cold clear early morning in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the stone and the stripes, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Cô Hạc Quán
places.size: A sealed ruined abbey of about 20 small grey halls on a forested ridge at about 300 m across, closed since the abbot sealed its door in a year of the fallen sects; empty, intact, locked.
places.where: Region 1/2, temperate forest at about 820 m on a ridge among bare grey peaks; on the map a jagged grey rocky country with pine forest and a meadow at the lower right. Former sect, held by Tùng Đào Cung, Wood, Metal 24 %. Nearest: Hổ Khiếu Cương 90 km, Thạch Khẩu Trấn 127 km, Quải Đài Lâm 135 km. The abbot's sealed door is not the school's to open.
places.imagined: A hushed noon. Twenty small grey halls stand in order with moss on their roofs, the abbey door is sealed with a great plain stone slab, and a single crane stands on the roof of the tallest hall.
places.subject: The place: Cô Hạc Quán, the Lone Crane Abbey, a sealed Daoist abbey on a mountain ridge. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a forested ridge among bare grey peaks and pine forest fills the frame, a green meadow at the lower right, thin scree between. The abbey: about twenty small halls of grey stone with moss-green grey tile roofs arranged in a tidy line along the ridge crest, a gate hall, a bell tower without a bell, cells in two rows, a small kitchen court, a herb garden gone to grass, a stone terrace in front, all intact and unlooted, courtyards swept by wind. Signature element: the abbot's door, set in the rear wall of the largest hall, is sealed with a great plain slab of grey stone mortared into its frame, taller than a man, with a faded red cord tied across it; beneath it the steps are untouched, with no footprints; on the ridge of the tallest hall stands a single large white crane, a bright speck against the grey. A narrow path of pale stone steps climbs from the forest to the gate. Wind-bent grass grows between the paving of the courtyards, and the roofs are crusted with pale lichen. Life at scale: no inhabitants; one tiny visitor sitting at the foot of the sealed door and a second at the gate. Light and season: hushed late-morning light in autumn, golden from the upper left on the grey roofs and the white bird, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Cửu Cao Phái
places.size: A minor beast-taming sect of about 15 riders and 50 grooms with about 200 cranes, founded 700: about 40 buildings (halls, stables, grooms' houses) on a wooded rise about 400 m across above a reed marsh, with about 8 crane-roost towers about 30 m tall; compact, with birds everywhere.
places.where: Region 1/2, the nine marshes of Dao Quang Lĩnh, temperate forest at about 310 m on a low wooded rise above reed marsh; on the map green meadows and pine woods with a river winding to the lower right, white-grey snowy mountains at the right and a blue bay at the upper right. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, Wood 31 %. Nearest: Lý Ngư Thôn 75 km, Hạc Tê Lâm 79 km. Crane riders carried the Pivot's messages in the rebellion.
places.imagined: Early morning. Slender red-lacquered crane-roost towers rise from the green reed marsh, each topped by a broad woven platform where great cranes preen, and the sky is full of riders circling, the cry of cranes never quite stopping.
places.subject: The place: Cửu Cao Phái, the Nine Marsh sect of crane riders, on a wooded rise above a reed marsh. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a green reed marsh with winding blue channels lies at the lower left and centre, green meadows and pine woods fill the left, a river winds to the lower right, and white-grey snowy mountains rise at the right with a blue bay at the upper right corner. The seat: terraces of pale stone climb a low wooded rise to a four-roof pagoda with grey tile roofs and red-lacquered pillars, the tallest outline; about forty buildings, halls with red pillars, long low stables and grooms' houses with open yards, feed barns, a training ground of trampled earth ringed with posts, a gate hall at the rise's foot; reed-thatch sheds on the marsh edge. Signature element: in front, in the marsh, about eight slender red-lacquered crane-roost towers thirty metres tall, each topped by a broad platform of woven reed where great cranes stand and preen, linked by plank walkways, and about two hundred cranes, white and grey with red crowns, standing in the shallows, perched on the towers, and in flight; a flight of six riders, tiny figures on crane backs, wheels over the marsh in a ring. Life at scale: grooms with baskets of fish feeding the birds, children with a young chick, boats poling through reeds. Light and season: early morning in spring, golden light from the upper left on the red pillars and the white birds, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Khai Dương Thành
places.size: A walled port city of about 26,000 roofs and perhaps 130,000 people, walls about 3.2 km by 2.4 km at a river mouth, with a sea mole and crowded quays; Thiên Xu's northern port.
places.where: Region 1/2, river mouth on the sea at sea level, temperate forest; on the map a deep bay of blue sea in the upper half, a forested headland at the upper left, a rocky coast at the lower right, a river winding down through the middle. Thiên Xu Tông city, founded 280, its gate rebuilt in 900. Nearest: Kiêu Minh Lâm beast lair 127 km, Thần Hi Lâm 146 km.
places.imagined: Pre-dawn. The great polished bronze disc on the east gate tower catches the first light before the sun, so the gate seems to burn while the streets below are still dark, and bakers, porters and ferrymen are already at work.
places.subject: The place: Khai Dương Thành, the Opening Sun city, the northern port of the great sect Thiên Xu. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep bay of blue sea fills the upper half of the frame with white wave lines, a forested headland at the upper left, a river entering from the lower middle in a sandy delta, a rocky coast with grey cliffs at the lower right. The city: a great rectangular wall of grey stone about three kilometres long with a dozen gate towers, enclosing some twenty-six thousand grey-tile roofs in neat rows and districts, a quay quarter with warehouses, an ore and timber yard on the river, a central market, a governor's compound, courtyard houses climbing the slope, and a sea mole at one corner running out into the bay with a lighthouse; river quays crowded with a forest of small masts, hundreds of barges and junks. Signature element: on the east side of the wall a very tall gate tower crowned by a huge polished bronze disc about eight metres across, the tallest outline, blazing gold as it catches the first light, a bright point of fire against the still-dark city; its beam crosses the streets in a thin gold line. Life at scale: porters with lamps in the dark streets, bakers' smoke, ferrymen casting off, crowds at the east gate waiting for the light. Light and season: pre-dawn in autumn, the city in blue shadow with golden light from the upper left striking only the gate disc, the bay, and the highest roofs, long soft shadows toward the lower right.
